html:
The Omaguaca were an Indigenous people of the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a long dry valley in Jujuy in northwest Argentina. The valley still carries their name.

They were farmers who terraced the valley sides and kept llamas, and they built hilltop forts called pucarás, such as the one at Tilcara. In the late 1400s the Inca Empire took over the valley and ran its road south through it. After the Spanish arrived the Omaguaca resisted for decades; their leader Viltipoco organised a revolt that was crushed in 1595. Their descendants merged into the Quechua speaking Qulla people of the highlands. Neighbours included the Atacameño to the west and the Diaguita to the south.
sum: The Omaguaca were an Indigenous people of the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a long dry valley in Jujuy in northwest Argentina. The valley still carries their name.
